decision.evidence_type: two joint all-SKU inspections with reversed image/region orders and renamed region IDs; disputed whole identities receive two focused per-view visible-part inspections

forward.prompt:
These are the eligible OVERVIEW photographs of one clothing SKU. Detail/closeup photographs have been excluded. Each VIEW contains its original photograph and SAM3 mask regions.
R001, R002, etc. are UNIQUE addresses of pixels, NOT garment identities. Different views ALWAYS have different region IDs. Match the clothing visually across those DIFFERENT IDs. Never require an ID to repeat across views.
Find each visually distinct garment with at least one usable region in EVERY shown VIEW. One garment may occupy MULTIPLE SAM3 masks in one view and ONE mask in another. A dress's bodice, waist panel, sleeves and attached skirt are parts of the SAME dress, not separate garments merely because SAM3 split them. A seam, change of transparency, pose or front/back appearance does not establish a different garment. Use the full photographs to identify construction and physical garment extent. In contrast, a separately visible shirt under a vest/jacket remains a distinct visual layer, even if sewn together. Matching color alone is insufficient. Mixed masks are not usable.
Only a visible portion is required in an overview; do not require full silhouettes. Keep repeated styling too when present in every shown view. Do not select by the item for sale. Do not invent new mask boundaries.
Return JSON only: {"reason":"brief visual comparison", "tracks":[{"garment":"description", "regions":["R001", "R004"]}]}. The IDs here are schema examples, not an answer. Each track must list actual supplied IDs covering EVERY shown VIEW, including all confirmed parts of that garment. Assign a region to at most one track. Unlisted regions are removed. If no garment is visibly supported everywhere, return an empty tracks list.
forward.raw: {"reason": "The blue jeans are consistently present in all three views, appearing in R001 (v0), R003 (v1), and R005 (v2). The other garments (white jeans, silver skirt, black shirt) appear only in one view each and do not appear in all views, so they cannot be tracked across all views. The blue jeans are the only garment visible in every view.", "tracks": [{"garment": "blue jeans", "regions": ["R001", "R003", "R005"]}]}

all_view_rule: Every eligible overview must support a visible part of the same garment. Closeups are excluded from both matching and context. No full silhouette is required.

identity.prompt:
Classify this retail photograph by its photographic composition, NOT by the clothing category or whether the full person is visible.
OVERVIEW: a normal front/back/side outfit or garment view, or a product-only photograph showing the overall object. A headless model, cropped legs, partial occlusion, or a small accessory filling the image does not by itself make a detail shot. A complete product photograph is an overview.
CLOSEUP: a deliberate tight detail shot of only a garment subsection, such as fabric, neckline, shoulder/back opening, fastener, label, waist or hem. The overall garment extent is outside the frame. These detail photographs are excluded from a later matching task.
UNCERTAIN: you cannot distinguish these photographic roles. Never guess based on file names or an item's title.
Return only JSON: {"role":"overview|closeup|uncertain", "reason":"brief explanation of the visible framing"}. Choose exactly one role.

The framing includes the entire product, consistent with an overview composition."}

explanation.reason: The image displays two full pairs of jeans from the back, showing the complete garment from waist to hem, with no close-up focus on specific details like fabric texture, labels, or fasteners. The framing includes the entire product, consistent with an overview composition.
